pool.text: Captain Henri Salaman established a military post in Niamey.
Governor Jules Brévié made Niamey the capital of Niger.
Niamey enacted its first city plan to relocate neighbourhoods and segregate populations.
A famine caused by low rainfall brought internally displaced people to Niamey.
The Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Niamey was founded in the city.
Niamey held its first municipal elections and elected Djibo Bakary mayor.
The French military base in Niamey transferred to the Niger Armed Forces.
The United Nations Economic and Social Council began solar power development in Niamey.
The Kennedy Bridge opened to connect both banks of Niamey.
Soldiers killed three student protestors during the Kennedy Bridge massacre.
Niamey became home to the country's first commercial radio station.
A coup d'état installed Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara as president in Niamey.
Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara was ambushed and killed at Niamey's airport during a coup.
Nigerian Yoruba immigrants ran seventy-five percent of Niamey's photography studios.
President Mahamadou Issoufou launched the Niamey Nyala initiative for the city.
American and French military bases were established at Diori Hamani International Airport.
The Niger junta began renaming colonial street names in Niamey to local names.
Local governments were dissolved and the mayor of Niamey was replaced with an army official.
Mutinous soldiers attacked government forces in an unsuccessful coup attempt in Niamey.
